proposed.explanation:
RANKING BY P/E RATIO (cheapest first):
1. ABUK ≈ 6.5× (annualised 9M EPS 8.74 → ~11.65; price 76.21)
2. EFID 9.4× (EPS 2.18; price 20.40)
3. TMGH 11.8× (EPS 6.98; price 82.50)
4. ETEL 11.9× (EPS 11.93; price 141.95)

RANKING BY PROFIT GROWTH (highest first):
1. ABUK +104 % (9M-2026 EPS 8.74 vs 9M-2025 EPS 4.28)
2. EFID +68 % (FY2025 net profit 2,695,301,670 vs FY2024 1,606,727,698)
3. TMGH +43 % (FY2025 net profit 18,201,981,482 vs FY2024 12,769,517,325)
4. ETEL −94 % (FY2025 net profit 578,063,000 vs FY2024 10,111,328,000)

NOTE ON ETEL: The reported net profit fell from ~10.1 bn to ~578 m EGP, yet EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93. This internal inconsistency (likely a share-count change or reporting reclassification) makes the profit-growth figure unreliable for ETEL. I have therefore weighted ETEL the smallest in the allocation.

NOTE ON ABUK: Only 9-month data is available; the P/E is an annualised approximation (×4/3). The 3-month EPS (1.99) and the 3-month change (662 %) are marked AMBIGUOUS due to OCR issues and were excluded from calculations.

SUGGESTED 4-STOCK ALLOCATION (100,000 EGP total):
• EFID  1,470 sh × 20.40 = 29,988.00 EGP  (≈30 %)
• TMGH    363 sh × 82.50 = 29,947.50 EGP  (≈30 %)
• ABUK    328 sh × 76.21 = 24,996.88 EGP  (≈25 %)
• ETEL    105 sh × 141.95 = 14,904.75 EGP (≈15 %)
• Cash remaining: 162.87 EGP

Rationale: EFID and TMGH get the largest weights because they show full-year, verified profit growth of 68 % and 43 % respectively at single-digit-to-low-double-digit P/Es. ABUK is attractive on valuation and growth but carries extra uncertainty from the 9-month-only data. ETEL is included for diversification (telecom sector) but kept at the smallest weight because of the unexplained profit collapse and the EPS/profit inconsistency.

No single position exceeds 30 % of the 100,000 EGP portfolio, well within the 50 % cap.

RISKS: All four are Egyptian-listed equities exposed to EGP inflation, interest-rate, and regulatory risk. ABUK's annualised P/E is an estimate. ETEL's profit trajectory is unclear. Past growth does not guarantee future results. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.

final.explanation:
CORRECTION FROM PREVIOUS RECOMMENDATION:
My earlier reading of ETEL's FY2025 net profit as 578,063 (thousand) was wrong. The evidence row 'Net profit for the year 22 578 063 10 111 328' with columns 'Note | 31/12/2025 | 31/12/2024' and unit L.E.(000) should be read as FY2025 = 22,578,063 (thousand) and FY2024 = 10,111,328 (thousand). The '22' is part of the 2025 figure, not a separate note number. This changes ETEL from an apparent 94% profit collapse to a 123% profit surge, which is consistent with the EPS rising from 4.79 to 11.93.

RANKING BY P/E RATIO (cheapest first):
1. ABUK ≈ 6.5× (annualised 9M EPS 8.74 → ~11.65; price 76.21)
2. EFID ≈ 9.4× (EPS 2.18; price 20.40)
3. TMGH ≈ 11.8× (EPS 6.98; price 82.50)
4. ETEL ≈ 11.9× (EPS 11.93; price 141.95)

RANKING BY PROFIT GROWTH (highest first):
1. ETEL +123% (FY2025 net profit 22,578,063,000 vs FY2024 10,111,328,000)
2. ABUK +104% (9M-2026 EPS 8.74 vs 9M-2025 EPS 4.28)
3. EFID +68% (FY2025 net profit 2,695,301,670 vs FY2024 1,606,727,698)
4. TMGH +43% (FY2025 net profit 18,201,981,482 vs FY2024 12,769,517,325)

SUGGESTED 4-STOCK ALLOCATION (100,000 EGP total):
• ETEL  211 sh × 141.95 = 29,951.45 EGP  (≈30%)
• ABUK  328 sh × 76.21  = 24,996.88 EGP  (≈25%)
• EFID  1,225 sh × 20.40 = 24,990.00 EGP (≈25%)
• TMGH  242 sh × 82.50  = 19,965.00 EGP  (≈20%)
• Cash remaining: 96.67 EGP

Rationale: ETEL earns the largest weight because it now shows the strongest verified full-year profit growth (+123%) at a reasonable P/E of ~11.9×. ABUK is the cheapest on P/E (~6.5×) with strong 9-month growth (+104%), but carries extra uncertainty from having only 9-month data (annualised P/E is an estimate). EFID offers a solid value/growth combination (9.4× P/E, +68% growth). TMGH is included for diversification (real-estate/conglomerate sector) with moderate growth (+43%) and a fair P/E (~11.8×).

No single position exceeds 30% of the 100,000 EGP portfolio, well within the 50% cap.

RISKS: All four are Egyptian-listed equities exposed to EGP inflation, interest-rate, and regulatory risk. ABUK's P/E is an annualised estimate from 9-month data. ETEL's 123% growth may not be sustainable; a single year of strong results does not guarantee a 7-year trend. Past growth does not guarantee future returns. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
